s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic painful intertriginous wounds with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques
Granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate with well-formed, nonnecrotizing granulomas
key_facts: 1.5-year history of painful intertriginous wounds
History of hypertension and depression
Multiple hospital admissions for cellulitis around the wounds
Received diverting sigmoid colostomy and indwelling urinary catheter
Received adalimumab for 3 months without clinical improvement
Family history of similar condition
Linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques in intertriginous areas
Wedge biopsy showed pseudoepitheliomatous epidermal hyperplasia and granulomatous inflammation
Histochemical stains, tissue cultures, and PCR for herpes simplex virus were negative
Elevated immunoglobulin G antibodies and flagellins

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and elevated immunoglobulin G antibodies

shortlist.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic painful intertriginous wounds and history of cellulitis

shortlist.label: Granuloma inguinale
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and intertriginous location of lesions

shortlist.label: Intertriginous granulomatous dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques in intertriginous areas

shortlist.label: Blau syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar condition and granulomatous inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques in intertriginous areas, along with wedge biopsy showing pseudoepitheliomatous epidermal hyperplasia and granulomatous inflammation, is most consistent with intertriginous granulomatous dermatitis. The lack of response to adalimumab and the absence of findings suggestive of other shortlisted conditions also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: Normal imaging studies of the gastrointestinal tract and lack of other symptoms suggestive of Crohn's disease make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and biopsy findings do not typically match those of hidradenitis suppurativa, which usually involves painful nodules and abscesses in apocrine-gland-bearing areas

rejected.label: Granuloma inguinale
rejected.why: The patient's biopsy did not show the characteristic Donovan bodies of granuloma inguinale, and the clinical presentation does not fully align with this condition

rejected.label: Blau syndrome
rejected.why: While Blau syndrome can present with granulomatous dermatitis, the patient's lack of other characteristic findings such as joint and eye involvement, and the absence of a clear familial pattern consistent with Blau syndrome, make this diagnosis less likely
